metadata.about: Round 730. Every row of public.ballon_dor, read by SELECT on 2026-09-30 (76 rows: 69 Men and 7 Women, rank 1 only, points and nationality NULL on every row), checked field by field against the co-organiser's own list (uefa.com, UEFA has co-organised the Ballon d'Or with Groupe Amaury, owner of France Football, since 2024) and at least one independent source on another host. Wikipedia is never a source here. Winner, year, rank and club were right on all 76 rows, so nothing is corrected; nationality was NULL on all 76 and the migration fills it. club is the club at the time of the award, as the official list gives it. nationality is the nation the player represented at the time of the award, written the way the site's other tables write it (Czech Republic, United States). points stays NULL: no reader shows it and nothing here verifies it. scripts/simBallonDor.mjs holds the migration's end state to this record.

metadata.method: Every row read from the live table with a SELECT on 2026-09-30 (md5 of id|year|winner|school|position|class over all 91 rows, ordered by id: 673fbd5b7f866475520cd118bc3de8dc). Each row checked against the award body (heisman.com/heisman-winners/, read from the raw page's per winner data attributes) and ESPN's all time list with positions. Year, winner and school were also read against ESPN's winners list. A value ships only where both sources agree; where they print the same person, school or role two ways, the note on the row says which form is kept and why. Wikipedia was not used.
metadata.positionRule: The award body's position code, which ESPN matches on 88 rows and prints as the same role on the other 3 (HB against RB for 1937 and 1944, CB/WR against WR/CB for 2024). Both sources list the running backs of every era as RB (two fullbacks as FB, two halfbacks as HB on heisman.com), the two way ends of 1936 and 1949 as TE, and give no second role to Kinnick, Horvath or Janowicz, so the table's era codes HB, E, HB/QB and HB/P were corrected to what both print.
metadata.classRule: class is not one of the verified fields. The 10 rows that carry one agree with heisman.com and are kept; the 81 empty ones stay empty rather than filled from one source.

metadata.adjudicatorWeb2026_09_15: Web adjudication, 2026-09-15, for the 18 pending Premier League rows. Two independent source families were read with WebFetch and WebSearch only: A, official (the premierleague.com squad data feed for season 2026, which lists a loaned-out player at his loan club and not at his parent, plus club, league and UEFA pages) and B, independent press (Sky Sports, ESPN, Sports Illustrated and others; Sky Sport Deutschland never counted as independent of Sky Sports UK). A row moved out of pending only where both families agreed on status and club. Each row carries its own URLs and read dates.
metadata.loanPolicy: A baked roster row has no loan concept: BakedPlayer is {n,p,a,v,r} and bakedToCMPlayer never sets onLoan or loanFrom, which exist on CMPlayer only for loans a manager makes inside a career (Rounds 71 and 506). The convention the repo already uses is to place a season-long loanee at the club he plays for: scripts/transferOverlay2026.mjs documents its loan field as informational, lists the club a player is playing for (Marmoush at Tottenham, ter Stegen at Ajax), and writes a loan that ended with the parent keeping the player as the parent club. The Premier League feed does the same (Mudryk absent from Chelsea 2026/27, present at Tottenham with loan 1). So Mudryk is movedTo Tottenham, with informational loan: true and loanFrom: Chelsea on the ledger row. The bake and harness read only name, from and to, so no code change is needed. The honest limit to record: in game he is a normal Tottenham player, who can be sold and does not go back to Chelsea at season end. A baked loan flag would be its own round (BakedPlayer, the bake emit and bakedToCMPlayer), not part of this data fix. A loan from a modelled club to an unmodelled one would be removedClubNotModelled with realClub naming both, for example 'X, on loan from Y'.

metadata.about: Round 708. The soccer_awards rows a game may read, winner by winner, checked on 2026-09-30 against at least two sources on two different organisations, the award's organiser wherever its page renders text. Wikipedia and other wikis are never a source here. scripts/simSoccerAwardsShape.mjs section 5 holds the live table to this record: every row of a verified award that passes the shape test must be a winner recorded here, every winner recorded here must be in the table unless it sits in knownGaps, and the List Quiz must deal exactly these names. year follows the table's own convention for each award, stated in yearMeans, and winner is the spelling the table holds (accents kept); the harness compares after folding accents and punctuation, so a source that drops an accent still agrees. shared marks a season two men won together. notAwarded lists seasons the organiser presented no award; the table holds a 'Not awarded' row for each and the shape test drops it, so the quiz deals nothing for those seasons. knownGaps lists seasons the sources have decided and the table does not hold yet: a migration adds them, and until it lands the quiz simply deals one fewer season. worldCupAwards is empty on purpose: the three World Cup awards stay on the DO NOT USE list until their record and migration ship in a later round.

metadata.usOpenFeed: https://www.usopen.org/en_US/json/man/past_champions.json is one feed for every US Open event despite the "man" in its path: fetched 2026-09-30 it carries 19 sections, among them ms (Men's Singles Champions 1881-2026, 147 rows) and ws (Women's Singles Champions 1887-2026, 140 rows), each row a year, champion, runner-up and score. There is no separate women's feed (json/woman/ and json/women/ both answer 404). The 140 US Open Women's Singles rows and the 2026 Rybakina fill were checked against the ws section of this feed, so the URL on those rows is the page that lists them. The ws section prints 2026 as champion Elena Rybakina, runner-up Aryna Sabalenka, 64 57 62; the ms section prints 2026 as champion Alexander Zverev, runner-up Ben Shelton, 63 76(2) 57 62.
metadata.nameVariants: The table stores some players under the name used that year and some under a later name: Margaret Smith and Margaret Court, Helen Wills, Helen Wills Moody and Helen Moody, Margaret Osborne and Margaret Osborne duPont, Molla Bjurstedt and Molla Mallory, Blanche Bingley and Blanche Hillyard, Charlotte Cooper and Charlotte Sterry, Dorothea Douglass and Dorothea Lambert Chambers, Kitty McKane and Kitty Godfree, Hazel Hotchkiss Wightman, Ann Haydon and Ann Haydon Jones and Ann Jones, Evonne Goolagong (Cawley), Chris Evert (Lloyd), Justine Henin (Hardenne). Each is the right player; the split is recorded here and left for a round that decides one display name per player.
metadata.score: The score column held no score on any row: 1,010 rows carried a three letter nation code (apparently the runner-up's, from a shifted scrape), 7 carried footnote debris such as "[ h ]" or "Peru", and 2 were NULL. No reader selects it. The migration sets every score without a digit to NULL. Every stored value is kept below under scores, keyed by id, read through the public REST API on 2026-09-30 from the same 1,019 rows the snapshot md5 covers, so the wipe can be reversed from this file alone.
metadata.notInScope: runner_up is NULL on every row, so Tennis Chain still cannot check a defeat; the official sources used here carry the runner-up and could fill it in a later round.

metadata.about: Round 661. Every fact the three hand typed trivia banks show a player (Hall of Fame or Bust, Guess the Year, Score Predictor), checked on 2026-09-28 against at least two sources on two different hosts, one of them the sport's governing body, league or hall of fame wherever that page would answer, and at least one that is not. scripts/simTriviaFacts.mjs holds the shipped files to this record word for word and fails if either side moves. Wikipedia and other wikis are never a source here. A fact that carries "noOfficial" stands on independent sources and says why the official page is missing. An entry marked "editorial" is a flavour line with no checkable claim (a Hall of Fame or Bust verdict label, a Score Predictor teaser hint) and says so. For Score Predictor, homeTeam is the side listed first: where one side really was at home it is that side, and "neutral" marks a final at a neutral ground, where the order is not a claim. Guess the Year uses the calendar year an event happened in, so a Super Bowl or bowl game played in January belongs to the new year. Round 661 fix: every Hall of Fame or Bust card also carries its real Hall of Fame record (hall), sourced like any other fact, with asOf on every 'not in' because that can change; a count on a card for a player still playing is a floor or carries asOf, the date it was last checked. www.fifa.com article pages turned out to be script shells with no text, so they count as no source and were replaced by readable inside.fifa.com pages. listQuizUclTopScorers holds the List Quiz's Champions League joint top scorers.
